subject: E-Commerce
title: The Decoy Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The Decoy Effect.

hook.text: A small popcorn is $3, a large is $7. Nobody buys large. Add medium at $6.50 and suddenly large sells out.

buildup.text: The medium is the decoy. It's not meant to sell—it makes the large look like a great deal by comparison.

discovery.text: SaaS companies use three-tier pricing for the same reason. The middle tier makes the high tier feel worth it.

twist.text: The Economist used decoys in subscription pricing. Adding a useless middle tier doubled premium sign-ups.

climax.text: Decoy pricing manipulates comparison. You think you're choosing rationally, but the menu was rigged.

punchline.text: The medium exists to sell the large. Decoy pricing rigs the comparison game.

quiz.question: What is a 'decoy' in pricing strategy?
options: An option designed not to sell but to make another option look better
